source: synthetic. Codex's first-run trust prompt, transcribed from Herdr's
        `trust_directory` rule (upstream/codex.toml) rather than captured: the
        prompt only appears the first time Codex opens a directory, and this
        machine's directories are already trusted. Sidecar had no rule for this
        screen at all before the manifest cutover.
why: it is the only upstream rule that reads `top_non_empty_lines`, so it is the
     one rule whose verdict depends on where the read window *starts* rather
     than where it ends. The window is the pane's own row count (pane_height),
     falling back to 24, so the same screen inside a taller pane and inside a
     scrolled buffer are different regions. See
     TestCodexTrustDirectoryPromptReadsFromTheTopOfTheWindow.
shape: the screen below is padded out to the declared 40 rows with blank lines,
       which is what `tmux capture-pane -p -e -N` returns: it pads the visible
       region to the full pane height and still terminates the capture with a
       newline. An unpadded fixture cannot catch the off-by-one that dropped the
       topmost visible row of every window, and this rule anchors on that row.
pane_title: sidecar-agent-status
pane_current_command: codex
pane_height: 40
state: blocked
screen:
> You are in ~/code/sidecar

  Since this is your first time here, Codex needs your permission before it can
  read or change anything in this directory.

  Do you trust the contents of this directory?

› 1. Yes, allow Codex to work in ~/code/sidecar
  2. No, choose a different directory

  Press enter to confirm or esc to cancel
